text: The report identifies |weight| >= 0.3 and a maximum of 50 genes as critical module-membership criteria.
quote: The strict membership threshold (|weight| >= 0.3, max 50 genes) was critical.
heading: Key Findings

text: Switching from D'Agostino K-squared selection to absolute weight thresholds replaced modules of 100-280 genes with weak cofitness signal (59% enriched, 1-17x correlation) with modules reported as 94% enriched and showing 2.8x correlation enrichment.
quote: The initial D'Agostino K-squared approach gave 100-280 genes per module with weak cofitness signal (59% enriched, 1-17x correlation). After switching to absolute weight thresholds, modules became biologically coherent (94% enriched, 2.8x correlation enrichment).
heading: Key Findings

text: Adding PFam domains and lowering the enrichment overlap threshold from 3 to 2 increased the annotation rate from 8% to 80% (92 to 890 modules) and yielded 7.6x more function predictions.
quote: Adding PFam domains and lowering the enrichment overlap threshold from 3 to 2 increased module annotation rate from 8% to 80% (92 to 890 modules), unlocking 7.6x more function predictions.
heading: Key Findings

text: The report contrasts PFam's broad annotation coverage with KEGG KO assignments, which it considers too gene-specific for module-level enrichment.
quote: PFam provides the broadest annotation coverage; KEGG KOs are too gene-specific for module-level enrichment.
heading: Key Findings

text: Module-ICA is presented as a process-level complement to sequence-based methods, not as a predictor of specific molecular functions.
quote: Module-ICA is **complementary** to sequence-based methods: it excels at identifying co-regulated gene groups (biological process modules) but should not be used for predicting specific molecular functions, where ortholog transfer is far superior.
heading: Key Findings

text: The decomposition produced 1,116 stable modules across 32 organisms, all with at least 100 experiments.
quote: **1,116 stable modules** across 32 organisms (all with >=100 experiments)
heading: ICA Decomposition (32 organisms)

text: The report describes module-size medians as 7-50 genes per module; it does not provide a single pooled median.
quote: Module sizes: median 7-50 genes per module (biologically correct range)
heading: ICA Decomposition (32 organisms)

text: Across the modules, 94.2% showed significantly elevated within-module cofitness by Mann-Whitney U test at p < 0.05.
quote: **94.2%** of modules show significantly elevated within-module cofitness (Mann-Whitney U, p < 0.05)
heading: ICA Decomposition (32 organisms)

text: Mean absolute fitness correlation was 0.34 within modules versus 0.12 in the background, reported as 2.8x enrichment.
quote: Within-module mean |r| = 0.34 vs background |r| = 0.12 (2.8x enrichment)
heading: ICA Decomposition (32 organisms)

text: Module genes showed 22.7x genomic-adjacency enrichment, reported alongside operon co-location.

quote: Module-ICA and cofitness show near-zero strict KO precision because KEGG KO groups are gene-level assignments (~1.2 genes per unique KO). A module with 20 annotated members typically has 20 different KOs.

quote: Ortholog transfer remains the gold standard for gene-level function prediction (95.8% precision), but Module-ICA fills a different niche: identifying which biological processes an uncharacterized gene participates in.
heading: Interpretation

text: The 6,691 predictions are explicitly qualified as process-participation predictions, not specific KO-function assignments.
quote: The 6,691 function predictions for hypothetical proteins should be interpreted as "involved in [biological process]" rather than "has function [specific KO]."
heading: Interpretation

text: As literature context, the report cites Sastry et al. (2019), *Nat Commun* 10, 5536, PMID 31767856, for independently regulated modules recovered by ICA from the E. coli transcriptome; the project's extension to fitness data across 32 organisms is the report's interpretation.
quote: **ICA for gene module detection:** Sastry et al. (2019) demonstrated that the *E. coli* transcriptome consists largely of independently regulated modules recoverable by ICA. Our cofitness-based approach extends this framework from transcriptomic to fitness data across 32 organisms, confirming that ICA captures biologically coherent co-regulation structure in phenotypic compendia as well. Sastry AV et al. "The Escherichia coli transcriptome mostly consists of independently regulated modules." *Nat Commun* 10, 5536 (2019). PMID: [31767856](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31767856/)
heading: Literature Context

text: As literature context, the report cites Price et al. (2018), *Nature* 557, 503--509, PMID 29769716, for mutant-fitness data revealing gene function at scale and for the association between correlated fitness profiles and shared biological function.
quote: **Cofitness as a proxy for co-regulation:** Price et al. (2018) showed that mutant fitness data across thousands of conditions reveals gene function at scale. Our use of cofitness (within-module correlation) as the primary validation metric builds on their finding that genes with correlated fitness profiles share biological function. Price MN et al. "Mutant phenotypes for thousands of bacterial genes of unknown function." *Nature* 557, 503--509 (2018). PMID: [29769716](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29769716/)
heading: Literature Context

text: The report warns that organisms with fewer than ~100 experiments produce weaker modules, although its example—Caulo with 198 experiments and 2.9x correlation enrichment—does not fall below that stated threshold.
quote: Organisms with fewer than ~100 experiments produce weaker modules (e.g., Caulo with 198 experiments showed only 2.9x correlation enrichment)
heading: Limitations

text: The component cap of <= 40% of experiments avoids FastICA convergence failures but may miss modules in low-experiment organisms.
quote: The 40% component cap (components <= 40% of experiments) is necessary to avoid FastICA convergence failures but may miss some modules in low-experiment organisms
heading: Limitations

text: PFam's coverage advantage carries a domain-level annotation caveat: functional associations may be overcounted.
quote: PFam-based annotations, while providing the best coverage, are at the domain level and may overcount functional associations
heading: Limitations
